chunks: The deliberate (killing) is in which he strikes with the weapon or the stick and does not desist from it until he kills; and the error is in which he does not intend it.

key_terms.السِّلَاح: Weapon — instrument of lethal force (sword, spear, knife)
key_terms.الْخَطَأ: Error, mistake — accidental killing requiring diya (blood money)
key_terms.الْعَصَا: Stick/staff — blunt instrument that can still constitute deliberate killing if used continuously
key_terms.الْعَمْد: Deliberate, intentional — the legal category of premeditated killing requiring qisas
key_terms.يَقْلَعُ: Desist, refrain — the attacker's cessation of the act before death occurs

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between deliberate and accidental killing in Islamic jurisprudence according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines the legal distinction between deliberate murder and accidental killing in Islamic law. Deliberate killing is characterized by sustained, intentional assault with a lethal instrument — sword or stick — without ceasing until the victim dies. Erroneous killing, by contrast, lacks any intent to kill. This distinction determines whether qisas (retaliation) or blood money (diya) applies.
